title: Developer Adoption, Fidelity Phasing & Cost Playbook
author: Maya Rodriguez
content:
Overview

This playbook defines a phased program for driving developer adoption of Redwood features while managing output fidelity and unit economics. It codifies objective rollout gates, pricing guardrails, telemetry to evaluate quality vs. cost, and prescriptive migration steps for customers moving from hosted to dedicated or private deployments.

Goals

- Accelerate productive usage by developer teams (time-to-first-success, sandbox-to-production conversion).
- Reduce cost surprises with staged fidelity increases and explicit billing communication.
- Protect user experience through fidelity gating and automated rollback on quality regressions.
- Provide a repeatable, instrumented rollout template for product and GTM.

Audience

- Product managers and PMMs planning feature launches.
- Solutions engineers and customer success running onboarding.
- Pricing and finance for packaging recommendations.
- Platform engineers implementing telemetry and rollout tooling.

Phased Roadmap (high-level)

1) Discovery & Sandbox (weeks 0-2)
   - Offer low-friction sandbox with starter fidelity profile (token-limited) and prebuilt prompt templates.
   - Telemetry: track time-to-first-success, prompt-template usage, early quality signals.

2) Guided Production Pilot (weeks 2-8)
   - Allow selected customers to increase fidelity in controlled increments with explicit cost estimates.
   - Run a 2-week quality evaluation using customer prompt set and Redwood eval harness.

3) Incremental Fidelity Expansion (weeks 8-24)
   - Expand fidelity by feature surface area or route. Enable per-route fidelity budgets.
   - Introduce optional paid fidelity credits for long-running pilots.

4) Full Production & Optimization (>24 weeks)
   - Encourage customers to adopt optimized batching/cache profiles and recommended quantization.
   - Offer Dedicated/Private deployment assessment if SLOs or isolation needed.

Rollout Gating Criteria (pass all to advance)

| Gate | Measurement | Threshold |
|------|-------------|-----------|
| Stability | Error rate (5xx) | < 0.5% over 48h |
| Latency | P50 response time | <= configured route SLO |
| Quality | Prompt-set pass rate | >= baseline - 3pt delta |
| Cost predictability | Average cost per 1k tokens | Within 20% of estimate |

Quality Evaluation Process

1. Customer provides 500–2,000 representative prompts.
2. Redwood runs automated evals (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity + human spot-checks).
3. If quality delta > 3 points versus baseline model, do not increase fidelity; create regression ticket.

Pricing & Packaging Considerations

- Fidelity Credits: short-term credit packs that let customers experiment at higher fidelity without committing.
- Per-route Budgets: customers can set monthly token budgets per API route that enforce fidelity ceilings when exceeded.
- Billing Transparency: show projected cost delta in Console before any fidelity change is applied.

Example console warning text (UX copy):

"Increasing fidelity for route /chat will increase average per-token cost by ~27%. Proceed?"

Telemetry & KPIs (what to instrument)

- Developer activation: time-to-API-key->successful-call (target < 10 minutes).
- Pilot conversion: % pilots that go to paid production (target 35% within 90 days).
- Fidelity impact: change in pass-rate for customer prompt-sets after fidelity increase.
- Cost delta accuracy: variance between projected and actual per-token cost.

Operational Playbook (step-by-step for SRE/SE)

1. Create a pilot workspace for the customer and seed with starter templates.
2. Configure fidelity gating: set initial ceiling = baseline_fidelity + 1 step.
3. Run evaluation job: run eval-harness against provided prompt set and collect metrics.
4. If pass, open billing change preview in Console and schedule the fidelity increase.
5. Monitor first 72 hours for regressions (quality, latency, errors). Rollback if any gate fails.

Rollback criteria (automated)

- If 3xx/5xx rate spikes > 1% absolute within 24h, auto-fallback to prior variant.
- If average prompt-set similarity drops by >5 points, trigger immediate pause and SE review.

Communication & GTM Playbook

- SEs: run a short pre-flight with customers explaining fidelity credit mechanism and show cost preview.
- PMMs: create collateral comparing fidelity bands with typical use-cases and cost ranges.
- Sales: use staged pricing add-on SKU for fidelity credits during pilots (30-day expiry).

Migration checklist (for customers moving to Dedicated/Private)

- Confirm SLO needs and traffic shape.
- Run capacity assessment using 14-day synthetic replay.
- Propose Dedicated sizing and fidelity profile (include quantization recommendations).
- Schedule migration window and rollback plan.

Example rollout snippet (JSON)

{
  "route": "/chat",
  "start_fidelity": "baseline",
  "target_fidelity": "high",
  "budget_tokens": "1_000_000",
  "monitoring_window": "72h"
}

Risks & Mitigations

- Unexpected cost overrun: mitigate with hard per-route caps and preflight cost estimates.
- Quality regressions from model swaps: mitigate with canary + prompt-set eval and human review.
- Developer confusion: mitigate via clear Console copy, inline cost previews, and SE-guided onboarding.

Ownership & Next Steps

- Product: Maya Rodriguez (program lead), roadmap alignment and definitions.
- Platform: Evan Chen (telemetry and gating implementation).
- Customer Success: Priya Kapoor (pilot orchestration playbooks).

Action items

1. Product to finalize fidelity band definitions and price multipliers (due 2028-11-14).
2. Platform to implement per-route budget enforcement APIs (due 2028-12-05).
3. CS to run 3 pilot customers through playbook and report back (start 2028-11-20).

Appendix: Fidelity band suggested defaults

| Band | Quality multiplier | Notes |
|------|-------------------|-------|
| baseline | 1.0 | Default free tier fidelity. |
| standard | 1.5 | Recommended for early production. |
| high | 2.5 | Use for critical low-latency, high-quality routes. |
| experimental | 3.2 | Short-lived exploration; require credits. |
